headline: AI Coding Agents Gain Self-Learning Skills for Reusability
summary: New GitHub repository enables AI tools to recognize and store successful coding strategies.
details: A recent GitHub entry introduces a framework enabling AI tools like Claude Code and Cursor to recognize successful coding strategies and store them as reusable skills. This development has implications for developers and engineering teams, as it could streamline coding processes and enhance productivity significantly.

The self-learning-skills repository allows AI agents to identify and harvest successful coding methods during a session. By capturing what it terms a 'hard-won golden path,' the system enables AI agents to not only learn from user interactions but also apply these learnings to future tasks.

The potential benefits of this technology are clear, but it raises an important caveat: the risk of over-reliance on AI tools. Developers might become accustomed to the suggestions made by these agents, potentially stunting their problem-solving skills in the process.

headline_marked: AI agent catches fake citations in 4 days [[on Qwen Cloud]]
headline: AI agent catches fake citations in 4 days on Qwen Cloud
summary: Developer creates AI tool to verify citations, tackling 'vibe citing' issue
details: A developer built an AI agent called CiteGuard that checks if citations support the claims made by other AI agents. The tool uses Qwen Cloud and provides verbatim quotes from sources to verify its findings.

The AI agent was created in just 4 days during the Global AI Hackathon Series. It works by fetching the source text and checking the claim against it, rather than relying on the model's own knowledge.
CiteGuard is open-source and available on GitHub under the MIT license. A live demo is also available at citeguard.boundy.workers.dev/demo.

The developer used TypeScript, Cloudflare Worker, and OpenAI-compatible DashScope International endpoint to build the tool. The project aims to address the issue of 'vibe citing', where AI-generated reports contain fabricated or misattributed citations.
